summary: Independent bounded read-only review of the current M4 snapshot/export implementation in the auditor worktree found two medium semantic defects: future verification affects past-asOf results, and SSP baseline identity can disagree with the configured assessment baseline. Both were reproduced using an isolated SQLite memory service. The two focused test suites passed all 35 tests.
coverage: Review subject: /Users/artem/visua/.check/evidence-auditor-20261013, base_head 2f82c73 plus integrated M3 and current M4 edits; baseline identity from auditor-worktree-baseline.json. Fresh bounded input contained requirements and source locations, without author conclusions. No source edits, live data, browser, PostgreSQL, Docker, Git, provider dispatch, or delegation.

Capture coherence: traced captureExportSnapshot through workspace atomic transaction and ws lock, post-lock workspace reload, revision/materialization, detached clone, full audit checkpoint, sorting and resource bounds. Inspected transaction context and VisuaService mutation/log lock agreement. Focused tests execute same-service mutation serialization, body hydration, invalid scope/time, limits and dependency closure.

Dependency closure: traced selected evidence, predecessor/successor traversal, recorded source checks and policies, missing-reference inventory and complete audit preservation. Read auditor-bundle.ts only to establish the consumer boundary and current/historical policy-byte availability semantics; this was not a bundle/verifier review.

Temporal and scope semantics: inspected current-record/no-historical-replay declarations, asOf parsing and future refusal, selected-framework enforcement, shared evidence acceptance/expiry/supersession, law effective-date scope, explicit exclusions, future-check filtering and verification timestamps. Current/target raw assessment values remain current records by explicit contract.

OSCAL: inspected SSP/POAM official-schema fixtures and sources.json, deterministic v5 UUID implementation, source pin constants and corpus manifest, implementation-level vocabulary, system identifiers, missing inventory labels, tailoring/exclusion disclosure, empty-scope refusal and generated schemas with actual formats. Explicit local not-implemented is permitted by schema TokenDatatype alternative and has truthful zero-level remarks; no finding on that representation.

Licensing and CSV counterevidence: PBC exports use Visua-authored requests and criterion references, emit only point-of-focus counts, and do not print licensed criterion text. Actual TSC ingest marks top-level groups and series unlicensed; readiness root titles therefore do not leak licensed criterion bodies in the inspected supported ingest. CSV quotes and formula/control-prefix neutralization are covered. General licensing policy for user-supplied artifacts was not inferred from model-routing restrictions.

findings.mechanism: When an accepted artifact predates asOf but requirement verification happened after asOf, snapshot-backed reports still classify the requirement as verified. scoreInput gates checks at asOf, and evidence validity gates acceptance time, but passes verifiedAt through unchanged; deriveStatus requires only a truthy verifiedAt. This introduces a future verification decision into the claimed evaluation-time status and verified-share metric.
findings.evidence: Executed isolated-memory reproduction: create valid evidence for PR.AA-01, retain its bound acceptance with reviewedAt/reviewHistory reviewedAt 2026-01-02, updateState current=target=3 and verifiedAt=2026-10-13T05:00:00Z, capture asOf=2026-10-12T00:00:00Z, render csfProfileCsv. Output contained Repeatable (level 3) — verified and Target met, verified, with valid evidence. Counterevidence: snapshot basis clearly preserves current assessment values rather than historical replay; that legitimately explains current/target retention, but does not make a recorded future verification true at the evaluation time. Existing tests cover acceptance and expiry transitions, not this future verification boundary.
findings.recommendation: Apply the same asOf boundary to verification signals used in effective status, retaining the original verifiedAt in raw snapshot data. Add a focused regression with valid earlier evidence and later requirement verification; before verifiedAt the report should not assert verified, and at/after it may do so. Preserve the explicit no-historical-replay statement.

findings.mechanism: The SSP reuses categorization.overall as its baseline identity before consulting settings.baseline. The service applies actual scope using settings.baseline and permits baseline updates independently through enableFramework. Once the two differ, the SSP identifies and hashes a different NIST baseline than the controls it exports, while the high-water impact categorization itself remains correctly recorded.
findings.evidence: Executed normal service sequence in SQLite memory: categorizeSystem with HIGH information impacts, then enableFramework with the same RMF settings except baseline=low, then capture and oscalSsp. Snapshot configuredBaseline was low; 149 LOW-baseline requirements were exported; import-profile href ended HIGH-baseline_profile.json and control-implementation.description asserted HIGH baseline. The configured baseline update is also exposed by the workspace.configure framework PUT route. Counterevidence: categorizeSystem normally sets overall and baseline together, so ordinary unchanged categorization passes current tests; tailoring is explicitly disclosed and no resolved-profile compatibility is claimed. Neither disclosure explains choosing the wrong recorded baseline.
findings.recommendation: Separate the selected baseline from categorization impact: derive profile href, baseline digest and baseline description from settings.baseline, while security-sensitivity/impact fields continue to derive from categorization. Handle missing baseline explicitly and add a regression where selected baseline and recorded impact differ.

limitations: Only the requested snapshot/export boundary and relevant dependencies were reviewed. Concurrent bundle/verifier/UI/app work was not independently reviewed; app.ts was read only to confirm framework-setting reachability.
No PostgreSQL, multi-instance capture race, full-suite, browser, live-data, backup/restore, or production operation was run. The lead owns those integration checks.
Official schema provenance and exact local bytes were checked against the committed source metadata and tests; upstream release assets were not independently downloaded during this bounded pass.
No claim of complete historical reconstruction, legal redistribution entitlement for arbitrary user files, absence of other defects, or independent authenticity of unsigned snapshot digests is made.
